description: We are from Uruguay, and we are interested in finding ways to use technology to help protect our country. Wildfires and unusual weather conditions can affect our forests, fields, wildlife, and communities, so we think it is important to understand how these events happen and how we can detect them earlier.
summary:
IGNIS UY is an interactive geospatial research platform developed by a five-member team from Uruguay for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Using NASA FIRMS observations from the MODIS and VIIRS instruments, our platform organizes and explores thermal activity records across Uruguay from 2000 to 2026.
 IGNIS UY combines an interactive historical calendar, 2D and 3D maps, exploratory satellite-matching methods, scientific reports, and research tools in one accessible website.
 Our approach investigates potential correspondences between MODIS and VIIRS observations using geographical grid cells, acquisition dates, spatial proximity, and temporal differences. We also introduce an experimental satellite–ground evidence workflow that explores how satellite observations could be compared with independent institutional and documentary records.
 The platform distinguishes thermal anomalies from confirmed wildfires and clearly identifies synthetic test data and unvalidated associations.
 Although quantitative sensor harmonization requires further calibration and validation, IGNIS UY provides a transparent, reproducible foundation for historical fire research and future evidence-based monitoring in Uruguay.
details:
Project Details — IGNIS UY

The Problem

Satellite observations provide valuable information about thermal activity across the Earth's surface. However, NASA's MODIS and VIIRS instruments differ in spatial resolution, detection sensitivity, acquisition times, and historical coverage.

These differences make direct comparisons difficult. Counting observations from multiple instruments without accounting for their characteristics can produce misleading interpretations of historical burning activity.

Our challenge was to create an accessible web application that organizes these observations, supports exploratory cross-sensor comparisons, and makes historical thermal activity easier to investigate.

Our Solution

IGNIS UY is an interactive geospatial research platform focused on Uruguay.

The application imports NASA FIRMS observations from MODIS and VIIRS, organizes them into a structured IGNIS Master dataset, and provides multiple complementary research tools.

Its main features include:

  • Historical Archive (2000–2026): Explore imported thermal observations by instrument, year, month, and geographical region.
  • Interactive Maps: Visualize the geographical distribution of observations using 2D scientific maps and interactive 3D representations of Uruguay and Earth.
  • Historical Calendar: Examine thermal observations by date and instrument to investigate temporal patterns.
  • MODIS–VIIRS Harmonization: Explore potential cross-sensor correspondences using spatial grid-cell coincidences and distance/time matching.
  • Scientific Quality and Sensitivity Analysis: Investigate the effects of spatial resolution, matching thresholds, missing records, and other methodological limitations.
  • Recent Monitoring: Request available recent NASA FIRMS observations using the official API.
  • Scientific Reports: Generate downloadable PDF reports summarizing observations, methods, results, and limitations.
  • Ask IGNIS: Interact with uploaded observations through a Python-based, rule-driven statistical research assistant.
  • Satellite–Ground Fusion: Experimentally compare satellite observations with externally supplied documentary and institutional records.

Scientific Methodology

IGNIS UY implements two principal exploratory approaches for investigating MODIS–VIIRS correspondences.

The first identifies potential coincidences between observations recorded during the same UTC day and geographical grid cell.

The second examines candidate observation pairs using configurable geographical-distance and acquisition-time thresholds.

Additional quality checks and sensitivity analyses help users understand how methodological choices affect the resulting associations.

These exploratory methods do not establish that two observations represent the same wildfire, nor do they provide a completed quantitative calibration between the instruments.

Our Main Innovation: Satellite–Ground Evidence

Beyond historical satellite visualization, our team developed an experimental satellite–ground evidence framework.

This component explores how NASA FIRMS observations could be compared with Fire Service/PAIF records and SINAE/MIRA institutional information using geographical location, date, time, and source provenance.

A controlled demonstration combines real NASA FIRMS observations with clearly identified synthetic institutional records to evaluate the matching workflow.

The demonstration establishes the operation of the software, but does not constitute independent institutional validation or evidence of improved early-warning performance.

Technology

IGNIS UY was developed primarily using Python and Streamlit.

Its technical stack includes Pandas and NumPy for data processing, SciPy for spatial analysis, Plotly and Matplotlib for visualization, Folium for geographical maps, Three.js for interactive 3D environments, and ReportLab for scientific PDF generation.

SGP4 and Skyfield support orbital calculations when appropriate orbital data are available.

The application uses NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS observations as its primary scientific data source.

Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure: SI tools assisted our team with software development, debugging, research, data-analysis methodology, technical documentation, translation, visual design, and presentation materials. SI-generated elements are identified in the project, with additional provenance information available in our GitHub documentation. NASA FIRMS observations are authentic satellite data, not SI-generated measurements. All scientific interpretations and project decisions remain the responsibility of our team.

Benefits and Intended Impact

IGNIS UY brings several research activities into one accessible platform.

It allows users to explore historical observations, compare instruments, inspect geographical patterns, export analytical results, and investigate potential relationships with external evidence.

The platform is intended to support scientific research, education, and the future development of more reliable monitoring methodologies.

Its initial geographical focus is Uruguay, but the underlying research concepts may be extended to other regions.

Limitations and Future Development

IGNIS UY is an independent research prototype, not an operational wildfire-warning system.

Its imported historical archive has incomplete temporal coverage, and raw observation counts have not been normalized for satellite observation opportunities.

Thermal anomalies are not equivalent to confirmed wildfires or unique fire events.

Future development will focus on improved historical coverage assessment, quantitative cross-sensor calibration, independently verified institutional evidence, and systematic validation of matching accuracy.

Our objective is to establish a transparent and reproducible foundation for understanding satellite thermal observations.

IGNIS UY — From Space to Ground Evidence.
